explanation: 'Loudly' tells HOW he speaks - it modifies the verb 'speaks'. ('Very' modifies the adverb.)

subject: English
q: 'Honesty is the best policy' - the word 'Honesty' is a/an:
explanation: Abstract nouns name things you cannot touch: honesty, bravery, love, happiness, wisdom.

subject: English
q: Which of the following is a demonstrative pronoun?
explanation: Demonstrative pronouns point at things: this, that, these, those.

subject: English
q: In 'The cat sat on the mat', the word 'on' is a/an:
explanation: 'On' shows the relation between 'sat' and 'the mat' - a preposition of place.

explanation: 'Happen' is the action/verb. Happiness = noun, happy = adjective, happily = adverb.

subject: English
q: 'Either...or' and 'neither...nor' are:
explanation: Correlative conjunctions work in PAIRS: either...or, neither...nor, both...and, not only...but also.

subject: English
q: Identify the interjection: 'Alas! He is no more.'
explanation: 'Alas' expresses sudden sorrow - a classic interjection, always followed by '!'.

subject: English
q: 'She herself did it.' - the word 'herself' is a:
explanation: Reflexive pronouns end in -self/-selves and reflect back on the subject: myself, yourself, herself, itself.

subject: English
q: Which of the following is an abstract noun?
explanation: Bravery cannot be seen or touched - it is an idea/feeling, hence abstract noun.

subject: English
q: In 'He is very intelligent', the word 'very' is a/an:
explanation: 'Very' intensifies the adjective 'intelligent' - words modifying adjectives/adverbs are adverbs.

subject: English
q: Which adjective-adverb pair is formed correctly?
explanation: Most adjectives add -ly: quick-quickly. Happy becomes happily (y to i), not 'happyly'.

subject: English
q: 'The jury gave its verdict.' - the word 'jury' is a:
explanation: 'Jury' names a group of people acting as one unit - a collective noun.

subject: English
q: Identify the conjunction: 'I stayed home because it was raining.'
explanation: 'Because' joins the two clauses and gives a reason - it is a subordinating conjunction.

subject: English
q: 'Which', 'who', 'whom' are:
explanation: Who, whom, whose, which, what introduce questions AND relative clauses - interrogative/relative pronouns.

subject: English

Her homework was already finished by her.

Her homework has already been finished by her.

Three novels were written by him.

A new car will be bought by me.

This problem is solved by her.

q: Change to passive voice: We should respect our elders.
options: Our elders should respected by us.
Our elders should be respected by us.
Our elders are respected by us.
Our elders must be respected by us.

q: Change to passive voice: He may invite us.

q: Which of the following sentences CANNOT be changed into passive voice?

subject: English
q: Change to passive voice: Shut the door.
explanation: Imperative passive: Let + object + be + past participle.

subject: English
q: Change to passive voice: Open your books.
explanation: Standard 'Let + be + participle' pattern.

Let your time be not wasted.

q: Change to passive voice: Did he write a letter?

Who was this book written by?

subject: English

subject: English
q: Change to passive voice: What are you doing?
options: What was being done by you?
What has been done by you?
What is being done by you?
explanation: Present continuous question passive: is + being + participle.

Where has this coin been found by you?
Where was this coin found by you?
Where were this coin found by you?

Why is he punished by her?

q: Change to passive voice: Which pen did you buy?
options: Which pen had been bought by you?

Which pen is bought by you?
Which pen were bought by you?
explanation: Singular 'pen' takes 'was'.

q: Change to passive voice: How did they break the lock?
options: How was the lock broken by them?
How were the lock broken by them?
How is the lock broken by them?
How has the lock been broken by them?

options: I was given a book by her.
A book was given to me by her.

Neither A nor B is correct.

q: Change to passive voice: The teacher told us a story.
options: Both A and B are correct.

q: The teacher said, 'The sun rises in the east.'

q: They said, 'We have finished our work.'

subject: English

He said that it rains heavily outside.
He said that it is raining heavily outside.

They said that they are going to play a match.
They said that they were going to play a match.

He said that he is going to buy a new car next month.

He said that he was going to buy a new car the following month.

subject: English
q: The doctor said to me, 'You should rest for a week.'

The doctor said to me that I should have rested for a week.
The doctor told me that I would rest for a week.
The doctor told me that I shall rest for a week.

subject: English
q: She said, 'I was writing a letter when you called.'
options: She said that she had written a letter when I called.
She said that she was writing a letter when I called.
She said that she is writing a letter when I call.
She said that she had been writing a letter when I called.

subject: English
q: He said, 'I had never seen such a beautiful sight before.'
options: He said that he would never see such a beautiful sight before.
He said that he had never seen such a beautiful sight before.
He said that he has never seen such a beautiful sight before.
He said that he never saw such a beautiful sight before.
explanation: Past perfect stays past perfect; no further backshift is possible.

subject: English
q: They said, 'We need not go there today.'

They said that they needed not go there that day.
They said that they need not go there that day.
They said that they did not need to go there that day.

subject: English

She said that he has been working there since morning.

The captain said that their team would win the match.
The captain said that our team would win the match.
The captain said that our team will win the match.

subject: English

explanation: 'Brave' describes the noun 'boy', so it is an adjective.

subject: English
q: Choose the correct synonym of CANDID:
explanation: Candid = frank and straightforward.

subject: English
q: Choose the correct antonym of EXPAND:
explanation: Expand = grow larger; contract = shrink.

subject: English
q: Fill in the blank: She was angry ___ me for my mistake.
explanation: 'Angry with' a person; 'angry at' a thing.

subject: English
q: Fill in the blank: He said that he ___ the match yesterday.
explanation: In indirect speech, past simple shifts to past perfect.

subject: English
q: Fill in the blank: ___ honest man is always respected.
explanation: 'Honest' begins with a vowel sound, so it takes 'an'.

subject: Urdu
q: Urdu qawaid ko ilm ke lihaz se kin do bunyadi shakhon mein taqseem kiya gaya hai?
explanation: Urdu qawaid ke do hisse hain: Sarf (lafzon ki saakht) aur Nahw (jumlon ki tarkeeb).

subject: Urdu
q: Ilm-e-Sarf mein kis cheez ka bayan hota hai?
options: Lafzon ki saakht aur tasreef ka
explanation: Sarf lafzon ki saakht ka ilm hai; Nahw jumlon ki tarkeeb ka.

subject: Urdu
q: Ilm-e-Nahw ka mauzu kya hai?
options: Jumle mein lafzon ka bahami rabta aur tarkeeb
explanation: Nahw mein jumle ke andar lafzon ke bahami rabte ka bayan hota hai.

subject: Urdu
q: Wo lafz jis ke tukre karne par us ka koi ma'ani baqi na rahe, qawaid ki ro se kya kehlata hai?
explanation: Kalma ba-ma'ani wahid lafz hai; us ke ajza be-ma'ani hote hain.

subject: Urdu
q: Kalma ki aqsam mein kaun sa lafz shaamil NAHI hai?
explanation: Kalma ki sirf 3 aqsam hain: Ism, Fe'l aur Harf; jumla kalma se banta hai.

subject: Urdu
q: Mehmal lafz se kya murad hai?
explanation: Mehmal be-ma'ani hota hai; muammal ba-ma'ani hota hai.

subject: Urdu
q: Muammal aur mehmal mein bunyadi farq kya hai?
options: Muammal be-ma'ani aur mehmal ba-ma'ani hota hai
Muammal ba-ma'ani aur mehmal be-ma'ani hota hai
explanation: Muammal = ba-ma'ani lafz (kalma); mehmal = be-ma'ani lafz.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Roti-shoti kha lo' mein 'shoti' qawaid ki ro se kya hai?
explanation: 'Shoti' ka koi ma'ani nahin, is liye mehmal hai.

subject: Urdu
q: Lafz 'aur' kalma ki kaun si qism hai?
explanation: 'Aur' do lafzon ko jorta hai aur khud mukammal ma'ani nahin deta - harf hai.

subject: Urdu
q: Lafz 'daurta hai' kalma ki kaun si qism hai?
explanation: 'Daurta hai' kaam ko zamane mein batata hai - fe'l hai.

subject: Urdu
q: Ism ki durust tareef kaun si hai?
options: Kaam ko zamane mein batane wala lafz
Wo ba-ma'ani lafz jo kisi shakhs, cheez, jagah ya sifat ka naam bataye aur apne ma'ani mein khud mukammal ho
explanation: Ism apne ma'ani mein khud mukammal hota hai; harf doosre ka mohtaj hota hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Lahore', 'Quaid-e-Azam' aur 'Ravi' ism ki kaun si qism ki misalein hain?
explanation: Ye khaas aur mutayyan naam hain - ism-e-ma'rifa.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Sheher', 'larka' aur 'darya' ism ki kaun si qism hain?
explanation: Ye aam aur ghair-mutayyan naam hain - ism-e-nakra.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Acha', 'bura', 'lamba' ism ki kaun si qism hain?
explanation: Ye khubi/kharabi batate hain - ism-e-sifat.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Mein, tum, wo, hum, aap' qawaid ki ro se kya kehlate hain?
explanation: Ye ism ki jagah istemal hote hain - ism-e-zameer.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Ye, wo, yeh, woh' kya hain?
explanation: Ye ishare ke liye istemal hote hain - ism-e-ishaara.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Kaun, kya, kab, kahan, kaise' kya kehlate hain?
explanation: Ye sawal pochne wale alfaaz hain - ism-e-istifham.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Jo, jis, jise, jinhon ne' qawaid ki ro se kya hain?
explanation: Ye do jumlon ko jorte hain - ism-e-mausool.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Jo mehnat karta hai, kamyab hota hai' mein 'jo' kya hai?
explanation: 'Jo' do jumlon ko jor raha hai - ism-e-mausool.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Sachchai', 'bahaduri', 'mohabbat' ism ki kaun si qism ki misalein hain?
explanation: Ye ghair-mahsoos cheezon ke naam hain - ism-e-ma'na.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Darakht', 'mez', 'kitab' ism ki kaun si qism hain?
explanation: Ye khud maujood cheezon ke naam hain - ism-e-zat.

subject: Urdu
q: Ism-e-Ma'rifa ki pehchan kya hai?
options: Khaas aur mutayyan shakhs, cheez ya jagah ka naam ho
explanation: Ma'rifa khaas naam hota hai, nakra aam naam.

subject: Urdu
q: Darj zeel mein Ism-e-Sifat kaun sa hai?
explanation: 'Zaheen' khubi batata hai - ism-e-sifat.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Ye kitab meri hai' mein 'ye' kya hai?
explanation: 'Ye' ishare ke liye aaya hai - ism-e-ishaara.

subject: Urdu
q: Zameer ki bunyadi khasiyat kya hai?
options: Ism ki jagah istemal hota hai
explanation: Zameer ism ka qaim-maqam hota hai.

subject: Urdu
q: Fe'l ki durust tareef kaun si hai?
options: Wo lafz jo kisi kaam ke karne, hone ya sehne ko kisi khaas zamane mein bataye
Shakhs ka naam batane wala lafz
explanation: Fe'l mein kaam + zamana dono hote hain.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Us ne khana khaya' mein fe'l kaun sa lafz hai?
explanation: 'Khaya' kaam ko guzre zamane mein batata hai - fe'l hai; 'khana' maf'ool hai.

subject: Urdu
q: Fe'l-e-Lazim kise kehte hain?
options: Jis ka fa'il maloom na ho
explanation: Lazim fe'l ko maf'ool ki zarurat nahin hoti, masalan 'wo sota hai'.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Bacha rota hai' mein fe'l kya hai?
explanation: 'Rota hai' ko kisi maf'ool ki zarurat nahin - fe'l-e-lazim.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Us ne seb khaya' mein fe'l kya hai?
explanation: 'Seb' maf'ool hai, is liye fe'l mutaddi hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Khat likha gaya' mein fe'l kya hai?
explanation: Fa'il maloom nahin, is liye fe'l-e-majhool hai.

subject: Urdu
q: Fe'l-e-Ma'roof ki pehchan kya hai?
explanation: Ma'roof mein fa'il maloom hota hai, masalan 'Ali ne khat likha'.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Ali ne khat likha' mein 'likha' kya hai?
explanation: Fa'il (Ali) maloom hai - fe'l-e-ma'roof.

subject: Urdu
q: Fe'l-e-Naqis kise kehte hain?
options: Jis se khabar ke baghair poora ma'ani na nikle
Jis ka fa'il maloom na ho
explanation: 'Hai, tha, hoga' naqis fe'l hain - khabar ke baghair adhoore lagte hain.

subject: Urdu
q: Darj zeel mein fe'l-e-naqis kaun sa hai?
explanation: 'Hai, tha, hoga' khabar chahte hain - fe'l-e-naqis.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Us ne khana khaya hai' mein kaun sa mazi hai?
explanation: 'Khaya hai' qareeb ke guzre zamane ko batata hai - mazi qareeb.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Us ne khana khaya tha' mein kaun sa mazi hai?
explanation: 'Khaya tha' door ke guzre zamane ko batata hai - mazi baeed.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Us ne khana khaya' (baghair 'hai' ya 'tha') mein kaun sa mazi hai?
explanation: Jis mein qareeb/baeed ka pata na chale - mazi mutlaq.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Wo khana khata tha' mein kaun sa mazi hai?
explanation: Jari rehne wale kaam ka bayan - mazi istimrari.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Agar wo aata to mein jata' mein fe'l kis mazi ki misaal hai?
explanation: Shart ('agar') par mabni mazi - mazi shartiya.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Kaash wo aa jata' mein kaun sa mazi hai?
explanation: Khwahish/tamanna ka izhar - mazi tamannai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Shayad wo kal aaye' mein fe'l kis taraf ishara karta hai?
explanation: 'Shayad' shak ko zahir karta hai - mazi ihtemali.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Wo roz school jata hai' mein 'jata hai' kya zahir karta hai?
explanation: Roz ka mamool haal ka bayan hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Kal wo Lahore jayega' mein fe'l kaun se zamane mein hai?
explanation: 'Jayega' aane wale waqt ko batata hai - mustaqbil.

subject: Urdu
q: Harf ki durust tareef kaun si hai?
options: Kaam ko zamane mein batane wala lafz
Wo lafz jo apne ma'ani mein doosre lafz ka mohtaj ho
explanation: Harf khud mukammal ma'ani nahin deta - doosre lafz ka mohtaj hota hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Se, mein, par, ko, tak' kya kehlate hain?
explanation: Ye ism ko fe'l se jorte hain - haroof-e-jarr.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Mez par kitab hai' mein 'par' kya hai?
explanation: 'Par' ism (mez) ko jumle se jor raha hai - harf-e-jarr.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Aur, lekin, magar' kya kehlate hain?
explanation: Ye do lafzon/jumlon ko jorte hain - haroof-e-atf.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Aye dost! idhar aao' mein 'aye' kya hai?
explanation: Pukarne ke liye istemal hua - harf-e-nida.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Nahin, na, mat' kya kehlate hain?
explanation: Ye inkar ke liye aate hain - haroof-e-nafi.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Hi' aur 'bhi' (masalan 'wo hi aaya', 'tum bhi chalo') kya hain?
explanation: Ye baat par zor dete hain - haroof-e-ta'kid.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Agar, jab' qawaid ki ro se kya kehlate hain?
explanation: Ye shart lagate hain - haroof-e-shart.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Sa, si, jaisa' (masalan 'chand sa chehra') kya hain?
explanation: Ye mushabehat batate hain - haroof-e-tashbeeh.

subject: Urdu
q: Harf aur Harf-e-Tahajji mein bunyadi farq kya hai?
options: Harf kalma ki qism hai jabke harf-e-tahajji alif-be ka har ek harf hai
explanation: Harf ma'ani ke lihaz se kalma ki qism hai; harf-e-tahajji sirf abjad ka aik harf hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Wo ghar tak gaya' mein 'tak' kya hai?
explanation: 'Tak' had batata hai aur ism ko jorta hai - harf-e-jarr.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Ali aur Ahmed dost hain' mein 'aur' ka kaam kya hai?
explanation: 'Aur' do ismon ko jor raha hai - harf-e-atf.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Mat jao' mein 'mat' kya hai?
explanation: 'Mat' mana karne ke liye aaya - harf-e-nafi.

subject: Urdu
q: Kalma ki teeno aqsam mein se kaun si qism khud mukammal ma'ani NAHI deti?
explanation: Harf doosre lafz ka mohtaj hota hai; ism aur fe'l khud mukammal hain.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Kitab ke liye' mein 'ke liye' kya hai?
explanation: 'Ke liye' maqsad batata hai - harf-e-jarr ki qism.

subject: Urdu
q: Wahid aur jama mein bunyadi farq kya hai?
options: Wahid aik aur jama aik se zyada
explanation: Wahid aik cheez, jama aik se zyada cheezon ke liye.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Larka' ki jama kya hai?
explanation: Alif wale muzakkar lafz aam taur par 'e' lete hain: larka-larke.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Larki' ki jama kya hai?
explanation: 'I' wale mu'annas lafz 'iyan' lete hain: larki-larkiyan.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Ghora' ki jama kya hai?
explanation: Alif wale muzakkar lafz ki jama 'e' ke saath: ghora-ghore.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Bacha' ki jama kya hai?
explanation: 'Bacha' ki jama 'bachche' hai - ye khaas qaida yaad rakho.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Qalam' ki jama (mukassar) kya hai?
explanation: Jama-e-mukassar mein shakl badal jati hai: qalam-aqlam.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Waqt' ki jama kya hai?
explanation: 'Waqt' ki jama-e-mukassar 'awqat' hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Shakhs' ki jama kya hai?
explanation: 'Shakhs' ki jama 'ashkhaas' hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Wazeer' ki jama kya hai?
explanation: 'Wazeer' ki jama-e-mukassar 'wuzara' hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Ameer' ki jama kya hai?
explanation: 'Ameer' ki jama 'umara' hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Nazm' ki jama kya hai?
explanation: 'Nazm' ki jama-e-mukassar 'nuzoom' hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Sabab' ki jama kya hai?
explanation: 'Sabab' ki jama 'asbaab' hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Ustaad' ki jama kya hai?
explanation: 'Ustaad' ki mashhoor jama 'asatiza' hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Mulk' ki jama kya hai?
explanation: 'Mulk' ki jama-e-mukassar 'mamaalik' hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Hakim' ki jama kya hai?
explanation: 'Hakim' ki jama 'hukkaam' hai.

subject: Urdu
q: Jama-e-Salem aur Jama-e-Mukassar mein farq kya hai?
options: Salem mein qaida qaim rehta hai, mukassar mein lafz ki shakl toot ya badal jati hai
Salem Arabi aur mukassar Farsi hai
explanation: Salem = qaide wali jama; mukassar = shakl badalne wali jama.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Mez' ki jama kya hai?
explanation: 'Mez' ki jama-e-salem 'mezein' hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Darakht' ki jama kya hai?
explanation: 'Darakht' ki jama 'darakhton' hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Dost' ki jama kya hai?
explanation: 'Dost' ki jama 'doston' aur 'dostaan' dono mustamil hain.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Sheher' ki jama kya hai?
explanation: 'Sheher' ki jama-e-salem 'shehron' hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Qalam' muzakkar hai ya mu'annas?
explanation: 'Qalam' muzakkar hai - 'kala qalam' kehte hain.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Chaadar' muzakkar hai ya mu'annas?
explanation: 'Chaadar' mu'annas hai - 'safaid chaadar' kehte hain.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Darwaza' muzakkar hai ya mu'annas?
explanation: 'Darwaza' muzakkar hai - 'bara darwaza' kehte hain.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Khirki' muzakkar hai ya mu'annas?
explanation: 'Khirki' mu'annas hai - 'khuli khirki' kehte hain.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Darya' muzakkar hai ya mu'annas?
explanation: 'Darya' muzakkar hai - 'gehra darya' kehte hain.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Kashti' muzakkar hai ya mu'annas?
explanation: 'Kashti' mu'annas hai - 'tooti kashti' kehte hain.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Pani' muzakkar hai ya mu'annas? (sochein!)
explanation: 'Pani' 'i' par khatm hone ke bawajood muzakkar hai - 'thanda pani' kehte hain.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Dahi' muzakkar hai ya mu'annas?
explanation: 'Dahi' muzakkar hai - 'khatta dahi' kehte hain.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Zabaan' muzakkar hai ya mu'annas?
explanation: 'Zabaan' mu'annas hai - 'meethi zabaan' kehte hain.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Awaaz' muzakkar hai ya mu'annas?
explanation: 'Awaaz' mu'annas hai - 'oonchi awaaz' kehte hain.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Suraj' aur 'Chand' ka jins kya hai?
explanation: 'Suraj' aur 'Chand' dono muzakkar hain.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Raat', 'Subah' aur 'Shaam' ka jins kya hai?
explanation: Waqt ke ye teenon naam mu'annas hain.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Haathi' aur 'Moti' ka jins kya hai?
options: Dono muzakkar (istisna: 'i' par khatm phir bhi muzakkar)
explanation: Ye mashhoor istisnaat hain - 'i' par khatm hone ke bawajood muzakkar.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Tasveer' muzakkar hai ya mu'annas?
explanation: 'Tasveer' mu'annas hai - 'khoobsurat tasveer' kehte hain.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Ghee' muzakkar hai ya mu'annas?
explanation: 'Ghee' muzakkar hai - 'khalis ghee' kehte hain.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Zaheen larka' tarkeeb ke lihaz se kya hai?
explanation: Sifat + mausoof ka murakkab - murakkab-e-tausifi.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Do kitabein' tarkeeb ke lihaz se kya hai?
explanation: Tadad batane wala murakkab - murakkab-e-adadi.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Maa-baap' tarkeeb ke lihaz se kya hai?
explanation: Atf se jura murakkab - murakkab-e-atfi.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Ali zaheen hai' mein 'Ali' qawaid ki ro se kya hai?
explanation: Jis ke baare mein kaha jaye wo mubtada hai; 'zaheen hai' khabar hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Subah', 'kal' aur 'aaj' qawaid ki ro se kya kehlate hain?
explanation: Ye waqt batate hain - zarf-e-zaman.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Iztirab' ka mutazad kaun sa lafz hai?
explanation: Iztirab (bechaini) ka mutazad sukoon (itminan) hai; ye jora recent papers mein aaya hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Dushman' ka mutazad kya hai?
explanation: Dushman ka mutazad dost hai; khasm bhi dushman ka mutaradif hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Subah' ka mutazad kaun sa hai?
explanation: Subah ka mutazad shaam hai; sawera subah ka mutaradif hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Tareeki' ka mutazad kya hai?
explanation: Tareeki (andhera) ka mutazad ujala hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Muhabbat' ka mutazad kaun sa lafz hai?
explanation: Muhabbat ka mutazad nafrat hai; ulfat aur wafa is ke mutaradif hain.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Shikast' ka mutazad kya hai?
explanation: Shikast (haar) ka mutazad fath hai; zafar fath ka mutaradif hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Jahalat' ka mutazad kaun sa hai?
explanation: Jahalat ka mutazad ilm hai; nadani jahalat ka mutaradif hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Ghareeb' ka mutazad kya hai?
explanation: Ghareeb ka mutazad ameer hai; fakeer ghareeb ka mutaradif hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Murda' ka mutazad kaun sa lafz hai?
explanation: Murda ka mutazad zinda hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Udaas' ka mutazad kya hai?
explanation: Udaas ka mutazad khush hai; ghamgeen udaas ka mutaradif hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Bad' ka mutazad kaun sa hai?
explanation: Bad ka mutazad naik hai; bura bad ka mutaradif hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Jhoot' ka mutazad kya hai?
explanation: Jhoot ka mutazad sach hai; fareb jhoot ka mutaradif hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Susti' ka mutazad kaun sa lafz hai?
explanation: Susti ka mutazad mehnat hai; kaahili susti ka mutaradif hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Tez' ka mutazad kya hai?
explanation: Tez ka mutazad ahista (sust) hai; chust tez ka mutaradif hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Thanda' ka mutazad kaun sa hai?
explanation: Thanda ka mutazad garam hai; sard thanda ka mutaradif hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Purana' ka mutazad kya hai?
explanation: Purana ka mutazad naya hai; qadeem purana ka mutaradif hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Bara' ka mutazad kaun sa lafz hai?
explanation: Bara ka mutazad chota hai; azeem bara ka mutaradif hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Tang' ka mutazad kya hai?
explanation: Tang ka mutazad wasee' (khula) hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Patla' ka mutazad kaun sa hai?
explanation: Patla ka mutazad mota hai; dubla patla ka mutaradif hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Door' ka mutazad kya hai?
explanation: Door ka mutazad qareeb hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Mushkil' ka mutazad kaun sa lafz hai?
explanation: Mushkil ka mutazad aasan hai; dushwar mushkil ka mutaradif hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Zyada' ka mutazad kya hai?
explanation: Zyada ka mutazad kam hai; kaseer zyada ka mutaradif hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Haram' ka mutazad kaun sa hai?
explanation: Haram ka mutazad halal hai; na-jaiz haram ka mutaradif hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Zulm' ka mutazad kya hai?
explanation: Zulm ka mutazad insaf hai; sitam zulm ka mutaradif hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Jang' ka mutazad kaun sa lafz hai?
explanation: Jang ka mutazad aman hai; harb jang ka mutaradif hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Barbadi' ka mutazad kya hai?
explanation: Barbadi ka mutazad falah (kamyabi) hai; tabahi barbadi ka mutaradif hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Sakhti' ka mutazad kaun sa hai?
explanation: Sakhti ka mutazad narmi hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Buzdili' ka mutazad kya hai?
explanation: Buzdili ka mutazad jurrat hai; dar buzdili ka mutaradif hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Na-insafi' ka mutazad kaun sa lafz hai?
explanation: Na-insafi ka mutazad adl (insaf) hai; zulm na-insafi ka mutaradif hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Bimari' ka mutazad kya hai?
explanation: Bimari ka mutazad sehat hai; marz bimari ka mutaradif hai.

subject: Urdu
q: 'Ghurbat' ka mutazad kaun sa hai?

explanation: Imam al-Shafii's al-Risala founded Usul al-Fiqh; he also wrote Kitab al-Umm.

subject: Islamiat
q: Kitab al-Umm was written by:
explanation: Kitab al-Umm is the major legal work of Imam al-Shafii.

subject: Islamiat
q: In Hanafi usage, a Wajib act differs from a Fard act in that Wajib is proven by:
explanation: Hanafis distinguish Fard (definitive proof) from Wajib (probable proof); both are obligatory.

subject: Islamiat
q: Sunnah Muakkadah is a practice that the Prophet (PBUH):
options: Performed regularly and emphasised; omitting it habitually is blameworthy
explanation: Sunnah Muakkadah is an emphasised regular practice; habitual omission is blameworthy.

subject: Islamiat
q: Mustahab (Mandub) means an act that is:
options: Recommended and rewarded, but not obligatory
explanation: Mustahab acts are recommended and rewarded, but not obligatory.

subject: Islamiat
q: Makruh means an act that is:
explanation: Makruh is disliked; avoiding it is rewarded, but it is not Haram.

subject: Islamiat
q: Mubah means an act that is:
options: Permissible and neutral, neither rewarded nor punished in itself
explanation: Mubah is permissible and neutral in itself.

subject: Islamiat
q: Khayar-e-Bulugh is:
options: The option to pay Zakat late
The option of puberty to annul a childhood marriage contracted by a guardian
The choice of a school of law
explanation: Khayar-e-Bulugh lets a person married in childhood by a guardian annul the marriage at puberty (with Hanafi conditions).

subject: Islamiat
q: The Iddah of a widow is:
explanation: A widow observes Iddah of four months and ten days.

subject: Islamiat
q: The Iddah of a divorced woman is generally:
explanation: A divorced woman's Iddah is generally three quru (menstrual cycles).

subject: Islamiat
q: Ushr on rain-fed agricultural produce is:
explanation: Ushr is 1/10 of rain-fed produce and half-Ushr (1/20) of artificially irrigated produce.

subject: Islamiat
q: Tasawwuf (Sufism) primarily stresses:
options: Purification of the heart and sincerity
explanation: Tasawwuf stresses inner purification, sincerity and remembrance of Allah.

subject: Islamiat
q: Wahdat al-Wujud (Unity of Being) is associated with:
explanation: Wahdat al-Wujud is associated with Ibn Arabi.

subject: Islamiat
q: Wahdat al-Shuhud (Unity of Witness) is associated with:
explanation: Wahdat al-Shuhud was taught by Sheikh Ahmad Sirhindi as a corrective to Wahdat al-Wujud.

subject: Islamiat
q: Sheikh Ahmad Sirhindi is titled:
explanation: Sirhindi is called Mujaddid Alf Thani, Reviver of the Second Millennium.

subject: Islamiat
q: Sheikh Abdul Qadir Jillani (RA), founder of the Qadriyya order, is buried at:
explanation: Abdul Qadir Jillani (RA) is buried in Baghdad.

subject: Islamiat
q: The Chishtiyya Sufi order in South Asia is associated with:
explanation: Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti of Ajmer spread the Chishtiyya order in South Asia.

subject: Islamiat
q: The Suhrawardiyya order was spread in Multan by:
explanation: Bahauddin Zakariya spread the Suhrawardiyya order in Multan.

subject: Islamiat
q: The Naqshbandiyya order is named after Bahauddin Naqshband of:
explanation: Bahauddin Naqshband was from Bukhara; the order bears his name.

subject: Islamiat
q: Ali Hujwiri (Data Ganj Bakhsh) of Lahore wrote:
explanation: Kashf al-Mahjub by Ali Hujwiri is the earliest Persian manual of Sufism.

subject: Islamiat
q: Imam al-Ghazali, titled Hujjat al-Islam, wrote:
explanation: Al-Ghazali (1058-1111 AD) wrote Ihya Ulum al-Din.

subject: Islamiat
q: The Muqaddimah, a pioneering work of history and sociology, was written by:
explanation: Ibn Khaldun (1332-1406 AD) of Tunis wrote the Muqaddimah.

subject: Islamiat
q: Al-Qanoon fil Tibb (Canon of Medicine) was written by:
explanation: Ibn Sina's Canon of Medicine was taught in Europe for centuries.

subject: Islamiat
q: The father of algebra, author of Kitab al-Jabr, is:
explanation: Al-Khwarizmi's Kitab al-Jabr gave algebra its name.

subject: Islamiat
q: Jabir ibn Hayyan is known as the father of:
explanation: Jabir ibn Hayyan pioneered experimental chemistry.

subject: Islamiat
q: Kitab al-Hind, a study of India, was written by:
explanation: Al-Biruni wrote Kitab al-Hind after studying Indian religion, science and customs.

subject: Islamiat
q: Ibn Battuta's travel account is called:
explanation: Ibn Battuta's Rihla records about 30 years of travel across Asia and Africa.

subject: Islamiat
q: The word Zam Zam literally means:
explanation: Zam Zam means to stop, from Hajar's (AS) words to contain the spring's water.

subject: Islamiat
q: Jannat-ul-Baqi, the historic cemetery of many Sahaba, is located in:
explanation: Jannat-ul-Baqi is the cemetery of Madina.

subject: Islamiat
q: Jannat-ul-Mualla is the cemetery of Makkah where is buried:
explanation: Hazrat Khadijah (RA) is buried in Jannat-ul-Mualla, Makkah.

subject: Islamiat
q: The title Israel in the Quran refers to which prophet?
explanation: Israel is the title of Hazrat Yaqub (AS); Bani Israel are his children.

subject: Islamiat
q: Bustan-ul-Muhaddiseen, a work on hadith scholars, was written by:
explanation: Bustan-ul-Muhaddiseen is by Shah Abdul Aziz Muhaddis Dehlvi.

subject: Islamiat
q: The first mosque built in Islam is:
explanation: Masjid Quba, near Madina, was the first mosque built in Islam during the Hijrat.

subject: Islamiat
q: Hajr-e-Aswad (the Black Stone) is set in which corner of the Kaaba?
explanation: The Black Stone is set in the eastern corner of the Kaaba.

subject: Islamiat
q: Maqam-e-Ibrahim, standing near the Kaaba, is a stone bearing:
explanation: Maqam-e-Ibrahim bears the footprint associated with Hazrat Ibrahim (AS).

subject: Islamiat
q: Wuquf-e-Arafat (standing at Arafat) takes place on:
explanation: Wuquf at Arafat on 9 Dhul Hijjah is the greatest pillar of Hajj.

subject: Islamiat
q: After Arafat, pilgrims spend the night at:
explanation: Pilgrims stay overnight at Muzdalifah after leaving Arafat.

subject: Islamiat
q: Ramy al-Jamarat (stoning of the pillars) is performed at:
explanation: Ramy al-Jamarat is performed at Mina during Hajj.

subject: Islamiat
q: The Hijri calendar era begins with the Hijrat in 622 AD and was formally instituted under:
explanation: The Hijri era was instituted during the caliphate of Hazrat Umar (RA).

subject: Islamiat
q: A Sahih hadith is graded highest because it is:
options: Authentic in chain and text, free from defect
explanation: Sahih is the top grade: continuous reliable chain, no irregularity or hidden defect.

subject: Islamiat
q: Which term describes a hadith whose chain is continuous back to the Prophet (PBUH) through reliable narrators?
explanation: That description defines a Sahih hadith.

subject: Islamiat
q: Fajr ki Sunnat-e-Muakkadah kitni rakaten hain?
explanation: Fajr ki 2 Sunnat-e-Muakkadah farz se pehle parhi jati hain.

subject: Islamiat
q: Isha ki farz rakaten kitni hain?
explanation: Isha ke farz 4 rakaten hain.

subject: Islamiat
q: Sone (gold) par Zakat ka nisab kitna hai?
explanation: Sone ka nisab 7.5 tola hai; chandi ka nisab 52.5 tola hai.

subject: Islamiat
q: Hanafi mazhab me Wudu me sar ka masah kitne hisse par farz hai?
explanation: Hanafi mazhab me sar ke chauthai hisse ka masah farz hai.

subject: Islamiat
q: Ghusl me naak me paani charhane ka hukm kya hai?
explanation: Hanafi mazhab me ghusl ke faraiz me kulli, naak me paani aur poore badan par paani bahana shamil hai.

subject: Islamiat
q: Fajr ki namaz ka waqt kab tak rehta hai?
explanation: Fajr ka waqt tulu-e-aftab tak rehta hai.

subject: Islamiat
q: Safar ya bimari ki wajah se jo roza na rakh sake, us par kya wajib hai?
explanation: Uzr ki wajah se chhuta roza baad me qaza kiya jata hai.

subject: Islamiat
q: Zakat-ul-Fitr ki miqdar gandum ke hisab se kitni hai?
explanation: Zakat-ul-Fitr gandum ke hisab se aadha sa hai.

subject: Islamiat
q: Najd (Riyadh) se aane walon ka Miqat kaun sa hai?
explanation: Najd walon ka Miqat Qarn al-Manazil hai; Madina walon ka Dhul Hulayfah hai.

subject: Islamiat
q: Tawaf-e-Qudum kise kehte hain?
explanation: Tawaf-e-Qudum Makkah pahunchne par kiya jane wala pehla tawaf hai.

subject: Islamiat
q: Sa'i ke dauran mard kis jagah tez chalte hain?
explanation: Sa'i me mard do sabz nishanon ke darmiyan tez chalte hain.

subject: Islamiat
q: Arafat me Zuhr aur Asr kaise parhi jati hain?
options: Asr ke waqt jama kar ke
Zuhr ke waqt jama kar ke
explanation: Arafat me Zuhr aur Asr Zuhr ke waqt jama kar ke parhi jati hain.

subject: Islamiat
q: Qurbani ka waqt kab shuru hota hai?
options: Eid ki namaz ke baad 10 Dhul Hijjah ko
explanation: Qurbani ka waqt Eid ki namaz ke baad 10 Dhul Hijjah ko shuru hota hai.

subject: Islamiat
q: Iman-e-Mufassal me 'wa kutubihi' se kya murad hai?
explanation: 'Wa kutubihi' ka matlab Allah ki nazil ki hui kitabon par iman hai.

subject: Islamiat
q: Namaz ka pehla rukn (shuru) kya hai?
explanation: Namaz Takbeer-e-Tahrima se shuru hoti hai.

subject: Islamiat

options: Teesri rakat me ruku se pehle
explanation: Hanafi mazhab me Qunut teesri rakat me ruku se pehle parhi jati hai.

subject: Islamiat
q: Tahajjud ki kam az kam rakaten kitni hain?
explanation: Tahajjud ki kam az kam 2 rakaten hain.

subject: Islamiat
q: Salat-ul-Awwabin kis waqt parhi jati hai?
explanation: Salat-ul-Awwabin Maghrib ke baad parhi jati hai.

subject: Islamiat
q: Umrah me Ihram ki halat me khushbu lagana kya hai?
explanation: Ihram ki halat me khushbu lagana mamnu hai.

subject: Islamiat
q: Zakat kin cheezon par wajib nahi hoti?
explanation: Zaroori istemal ke ghar ke saman par Zakat wajib nahi hoti.

subject: Islamiat
q: Nabi (PBUH) ki shadi Hazrat Khadijah (RA) se kis umar me hui?
explanation: Nabi (PBUH) ki shadi 25 saal ki umar me Hazrat Khadijah (RA) se hui.

subject: Islamiat
q: Hazrat Khadijah (RA) ki umar shadi ke waqt kitni thi?
explanation: Hazrat Khadijah (RA) ki umar shadi ke waqt 40 saal thi.

subject: Islamiat
q: Nabi (PBUH) ke sab se pehle bete ka naam kya tha?
explanation: Nabi (PBUH) ke pehle bete Qasim the; isi liye aap ki kuniyat Abul Qasim hai.

q: Nabi (PBUH) ki sab se chhoti beti kaun theen?
explanation: Sab se chhoti beti Hazrat Fatima (RA) theen.

subject: Islamiat
q: Pehli khatoon Musalman kaun theen?
explanation: Sab se pehle Islam qabool karne wali khatoon Hazrat Khadijah (RA) theen.

subject: Islamiat

explanation: Baligh mardon me sab se pehle Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) ne Islam qabool kiya.

subject: Islamiat
q: Makkah me khufiya dawat ka markaz kaun sa ghar tha?
explanation: Khufiya dawat ka markaz Hazrat Arqam (RA) ka ghar (Dar-e-Arqam) tha.

subject: Islamiat
q: Banu Hashim ka muqata (boycott) taqreeban kitne saal raha?
explanation: Shi'b Abi Talib ka boycott taqreeban 3 saal raha.

subject: Islamiat
q: Madina pahunch kar Nabi (PBUH) ne sab se pehle qiyam kis ke ghar kiya?
explanation: Madina me Nabi (PBUH) ne pehle Hazrat Abu Ayyub Ansari (RA) ke ghar qiyam kiya.

subject: Islamiat
q: Muhajirun aur Ansar ke darmiyan bhai-chara (Mawakhat) kahan qaim hua?
explanation: Mawakhat Madina me Muhajirun aur Ansar ke darmiyan qaim hui.

subject: Islamiat
q: Ghar-e-Hira kis pahar par hai?
explanation: Ghar-e-Hira Jabal al-Noor par hai.

subject: Islamiat

explanation: Ibteda me 50 namazen farz huin, phir takhfeef ke baad 5 reh gain.

q: Ghazwa-e-Badr me Musalmanon ke paas kitne ghore the?
explanation: Badr me Musalmanon ke paas sirf 2 ghore aur 70 oont the.

subject: Islamiat

explanation: Uhud me Hazrat Hamza (RA) shaheed hue; unhe Sayyid-ush-Shuhada kehte hain.

subject: Islamiat
q: 'Ahzab' ka lafzi matlab kya hai?
explanation: Ahzab ka matlab giroh hai; Khandaq ko Ghazwa-e-Ahzab bhi kehte hain.

subject: Islamiat

explanation: Hudaibiya ke waqt Musalman taqreeban 1400 the.

explanation: Muta me tartib Zaid, phir Jafar, phir Abdullah bin Rawaha thi.

subject: Islamiat

explanation: Jo Abu Sufyan ke ghar dakhil ho gaya, use aman di gayi.

subject: Islamiat

explanation: Masjid-e-Zirar (masjid-e-zarar) ko Tabuk se wapsi par girane ka hukm hua.

subject: Islamiat
q: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) ko 'Atiq' ka laqab kyun diya gaya?
options: Un ki tijarat ki wajah se
Aag se aazadi ki basharat ki wajah se
Un ke qabile ki wajah se
Un ki shujaat ki wajah se
explanation: Atiq ka matlab aag se aazad; Nabi (PBUH) ne Abu Bakr ko ye basharat di thi.

subject: Islamiat
q: Taraweeh ki ba-jamaat namaz ka nizam kis Khalifa ne bahal kiya?
explanation: Hazrat Umar (RA) ne Taraweeh ba-jamaat ka nizam bahal kiya.

subject: Islamiat
q: Hazrat Umar (RA) ki shahadat kis namaz ke dauran hui?
explanation: Hazrat Umar (RA) par Fajr ki namaz ke dauran hamla hua.

subject: Islamiat
q: Abu Lulu (Hazrat Umar ke qatil) kis ka ghulam tha?
explanation: Abu Lulu Mughira bin Shuba ka ghulam tha.

subject: Islamiat
q: Basra sheher ki bunyad kis ne rakhi?
explanation: Basra ki bunyad Hazrat Utba bin Ghazwan (RA) ne rakhi.

subject: Islamiat
q: Hazrat Usman (RA) ki pehli zauja kon theen?
explanation: Hazrat Usman (RA) ki pehli zauja Hazrat Ruqayya (RA) theen, Nabi (PBUH) ki beti.

subject: Islamiat
q: Hazrat Ali (RA) ke walid ka naam kya tha?
explanation: Hazrat Ali (RA) ke walid Abu Talib the.

explanation: Hazrat Ali (RA) ki pehli zauja Hazrat Fatima (RA) theen.

subject: Islamiat
q: Jang-e-Jamal me 'Jamal' ka matlab kya hai?
explanation: Jamal ka matlab oont hai; ye jang Hazrat Aisha (RA) ke oont ki nisbat se mashhoor hui.

subject: Islamiat

explanation: Ibn Muljim ka talluq Khawarij se tha.

subject: Islamiat
q: Ashra Mubashra me sab se aakhir me wafat kis ki hui?
explanation: Ashra Mubashra me sab se aakhir me Saad bin Abi Waqqas (RA) ki wafat hui.

subject: Islamiat
q: Saad bin Abi Waqqas ne kis umar me Islam qabool kiya?
explanation: Saad bin Abi Waqqas ne 17 saal ki umar me Islam qabool kiya.

subject: Islamiat
q: Madina me Hazrat Abdur Rahman bin Auf se Mawakhat kis ki hui?
explanation: Abdur Rahman bin Auf ki Mawakhat Saad bin Rabi se hui.

subject: Islamiat

explanation: Zubair bin Awam ko Hawari-e-Rasool (Rasool ka madadgar) kehte hain.

subject: Islamiat

explanation: Uhud me Nabi (PBUH) ki hifazat par Talha ko Talha al-Khair kaha gaya.

subject: Islamiat
q: Taun-e-Amwas kis ilaqe me phaila tha?
explanation: Taun-e-Amwas Sham ke ilaqe me phaila tha.

subject: Islamiat
q: Hazrat Abu Huraira (RA) ne taqreeban kitne saal Nabi (PBUH) ki suhbat me guzare?
explanation: Abu Huraira (RA) ne taqreeban 4 saal Nabi (PBUH) ki suhbat me guzare, phir bhi sab se zyada Ahadis riwayat ki.

subject: Islamiat
q: Wafat-e-Nabi (PBUH) ke waqt Hazrat Ibn Abbas (RA) ki umar taqreeban kitni thi?
explanation: Wafat ke waqt Ibn Abbas (RA) ki umar taqreeban 13 saal thi.

subject: Islamiat
q: Hazrat Salman Farsi (RA) ka asal watan kahan tha?
explanation: Salman Farsi ka asal watan Fars (Persia) tha.

subject: Islamiat
q: Quran-e-Pak me kul kitne Ruku hain?
explanation: Quran me kul 540 Ruku hain.

subject: Islamiat
q: Quran ke alfaz taqreeban kitne hain?
explanation: Quran ke alfaz taqreeban 77,430 hain; Ayaat 6,236 hain.

subject: Islamiat
q: Surah Baqarah ki aakhri do ayaat kis naam se mashhoor hain?
explanation: Surah Baqarah ki aakhri do ayaat 'Amanar Rasool' se shuru hoti hain.

subject: Islamiat
q: Surah Kahf ki ibtedai ayaat ki fazilat kya bayan hui?
explanation: Surah Kahf ki pehli 10 ayaat Dajjal ke fitne se hifazat ka zariya bayan hui hain.

subject: Islamiat
q: Quran ki sab se azeem Ayat kaun si mani jati hai?
explanation: Ayat-ul-Kursi (Baqarah: 255) Quran ki sab se azeem Ayat mani jati hai.

subject: Islamiat
q: Quran me sab se zyada zikr kis nabi ka hua hai?
explanation: Quran me sab se zyada Hazrat Musa (AS) ka zikr hua hai.

subject: Islamiat
q: Surah Nasr kis mauqe par nazil hui?
explanation: Surah Nasr Fatah Makkah ke baad nazil hui aur fatah ki basharat deti hai.

subject: Islamiat
q: Surah Lahab kis shakhs ke bare me nazil hui?
explanation: Surah Lahab Abu Lahab ke bare me nazil hui.

subject: Islamiat
q: Surah Kausar ke nuzul ka pas-e-manzar kya tha?

explanation: Surah Kausar dushmanon ke 'abtar' (nasal kati hui) ke taane ke jawab me nazil hui.

subject: Islamiat

explanation: Ayat-e-Mubahila Surah Aale Imran me hai.

subject: Islamiat
q: Ashab-e-Kahf kitne saal soye rahe?
explanation: Ashab-e-Kahf 309 saal soye rahe (Surah Kahf).

subject: Islamiat
q: Surah Yusuf ke mutabiq Hazrat Yusuf (AS) ke kitne bhai the?
explanation: Hazrat Yusuf (AS) ke 11 bhai the; khwab me 11 sitare dekhe the.

subject: Islamiat

explanation: Surah Hijr (15:9) me Allah ne Quran ki hifazat ka wada farmaya hai.

subject: Islamiat

explanation: Tarteel ka matlab theher theher kar wazeh tor par Quran parhna hai.

subject: Islamiat
q: Surah Mulk ki fazilat ke mutabiq wo kis azab se bachati hai?
explanation: Surah Mulk ki tilawat qabr ke azab se bachao ka zariya bayan hui hai.

subject: Islamiat

explanation: Surah Sajda ko Alif Lam Mim Tanzil bhi kehte hain.

subject: Islamiat

explanation: Samad ka matlab wo be-niyaz hai; sab us ke muhtaj hain, wo kisi ka muhtaj nahi.

explanation: Surah Rahman (55) ke baad Surah Waqia (56) aati hai.

subject: Islamiat

explanation: Abdur Rahman I ko Saqr Quraysh (Quraysh ka baaz) kehte hain.

subject: Islamiat

explanation: Cordoba ki jama masjid ki tameer Abdur Rahman I ne shuru karwai.

explanation: Usman I ke baad us ka beta Orhan hukmaran bana.

subject: Islamiat

explanation: Babur ke baad us ka beta Humayun takht par baitha.

explanation: Jabal Tariq ka matlab Tariq ka pahar hai; Tariq bin Ziyad 711 me wahan utra tha.

subject: Islamiat

subject: Islamiat

subject: Islamiat

subject: Everyday Science
q: One joule is equal to:
explanation: Work = force x distance, so 1 joule = 1 newton x 1 metre.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The kinetic energy of a moving body is given by:
explanation: Kinetic energy = 1/2 mv2, where m is mass and v is velocity.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The potential energy of a body of mass m at height h is:
explanation: Gravitational potential energy = mgh, where g is the acceleration due to gravity.

subject: Everyday Science
q: If the velocity of a body is doubled, its kinetic energy becomes:
explanation: Kinetic energy depends on v2, so doubling v makes the energy 2^2 = 4 times.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Energy can neither be created nor destroyed; it can only be changed from one form to another. This is the:
explanation: This is the law of conservation of energy, a fundamental principle of physics.

subject: Everyday Science
q: A stretched bow (ready to shoot an arrow) mainly possesses:
explanation: A stretched bow stores elastic potential energy, which becomes kinetic energy when released.

subject: Everyday Science
q: A solar cell converts light energy directly into:
explanation: A solar cell (photovoltaic cell) converts light energy into electrical energy.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Water stored behind a dam mainly possesses:
explanation: Stored water at a height has gravitational potential energy, which is converted to kinetic and then electrical energy.

subject: Everyday Science
q: A machine does 600 joules of work in 20 seconds. Its power is:
explanation: Power = work / time = 600 / 20 = 30 watts.

subject: Everyday Science
q: A machine with 80 percent efficiency is given 100 joules of input energy. Its useful output is:
explanation: Efficiency = useful output / input, so 80 percent of 100 J = 80 J of useful output.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Which of the following is NOT a form of energy?
explanation: Friction is a force, not a form of energy; heat, light and sound are forms of energy.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Light travels fastest in:
explanation: Light travels fastest in a vacuum (about 300,000 km/s) and slows down in denser media.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The speed of light in water is approximately:
explanation: Light slows to about 225,000 km/s in water (speed in vacuum divided by the refractive index 1.33).

subject: Everyday Science
q: According to the law of reflection:
options: The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection
The angle of reflection is always zero
Light bends away from the normal
The angle of incidence is double the angle of reflection
explanation: In reflection the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, measured from the normal.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The image formed by a plane mirror is:
options: Virtual and of the same size
explanation: A plane mirror forms a virtual, upright image of the same size, laterally inverted.

subject: Everyday Science
q: When light passes from air into glass, it bends:
explanation: Going from a rarer medium (air) to a denser one (glass), light bends toward the normal.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Total internal reflection occurs when light travels from a denser to a rarer medium at an angle:
explanation: Beyond the critical angle, light cannot leave the denser medium and is totally reflected back.

subject: Everyday Science
q: A mirage (shimmering water on a hot road) is caused by:
explanation: Hot air layers near the ground refract light until total internal reflection occurs, creating a mirage.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The splitting of white light into its constituent colours is called:
explanation: Dispersion splits white light into seven colours, as seen in a prism or a rainbow.

subject: Everyday Science
q: When white light passes through a prism, it splits into how many colours?
explanation: A prism disperses white light into seven colours: violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange and red (VIBGYOR).

subject: Everyday Science
q: A rainbow is formed when sunlight passes through:
explanation: Raindrops act like tiny prisms: they refract, disperse and reflect sunlight to form a rainbow.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The sky appears blue mainly because of the ___ of sunlight by air molecules.
explanation: Air molecules scatter blue light much more than other colours (Rayleigh scattering), so the sky looks blue.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The primary colours of light are:
explanation: The primary colours of light are red, green and blue; together they make white light.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Long-sight (hypermetropia) is corrected by using a ___ lens.
explanation: Hypermetropia is corrected with a convex (converging) lens, which brings the focus forward onto the retina.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Short-sight (myopia) is corrected by using a ___ lens.
explanation: Myopia is corrected with a concave (diverging) lens, which moves the focus back onto the retina.

subject: Everyday Science
q: By the sign convention used in textbooks, the focal length of a concave mirror is:
explanation: A concave mirror converges light in front of it, so its focal length is taken as negative.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Sound waves in air are:
explanation: Sound travels in air as a longitudinal wave: particles vibrate along the direction of travel.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Sound travels fastest in:
explanation: Sound travels fastest in solids: about 5,000 m/s in steel, 1,500 m/s in water and 343 m/s in air.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The speed of sound in air at about 20 C is approximately:
explanation: Sound travels at about 343 m/s in air at 20 C; it is much faster in water and steel.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Sound cannot travel through a:
explanation: Sound needs a medium, so it cannot travel through a vacuum; this is why space is silent.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The pitch of a sound depends mainly on its:
explanation: Higher frequency means higher pitch; a shrill voice has a higher frequency than a deep voice.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The loudness of a sound depends mainly on its:
explanation: Greater amplitude means a louder sound; frequency controls pitch, not loudness.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The unit used to measure the loudness (intensity level) of sound is the:
explanation: Sound intensity level is measured in decibels (dB); frequency is measured in hertz.

subject: Everyday Science
q: An echo is produced by the ___ of sound from a distant surface.
explanation: An echo is a reflected sound that returns to the listener after striking a surface.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Ultrasound has a frequency above:
explanation: Sounds above 20,000 Hz are ultrasound; humans cannot hear them, but bats and dolphins use them.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Bats find their way in the dark by using:
explanation: Bats emit ultrasound and listen for the echo (echolocation) to locate objects and prey.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The same note played on a sitar and a flute sounds different because of a difference in:
explanation: Timbre (quality) depends on the overtones of the sound, so different instruments sound different at the same pitch.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Heat can be transferred from the Sun to the Earth without any medium by:
explanation: Radiation needs no medium; sunlight travels through the vacuum of space by radiation.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Heat is mainly transferred through a metal rod by:
explanation: In solids, heat travels by conduction: vibrating particles pass energy to their neighbours.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Heat is transferred through liquids and gases mainly by:
explanation: In fluids, warm parts rise and cool parts sink, carrying heat by convection.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Water has its maximum density at:
explanation: Water is densest at 4 C; below this it expands as it cools, which is why ice floats.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Ice floats on water because:
options: Ice is less dense than water
Ice has more mass than water
explanation: Ice is about 9 percent less dense than water, so it floats with most of its volume submerged.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The heat required to change ice at 0 C into water at 0 C (without any temperature change) is called:
explanation: Latent heat is the heat absorbed or released during a change of state at constant temperature.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Which of the following has the highest specific heat capacity?
explanation: Water has a very high specific heat (about 4,200 J/kg K), so it heats and cools slowly.

subject: Everyday Science
q: A thermometer is used to measure:
explanation: A thermometer measures temperature; heat is energy, measured in joules.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Ohm's law is expressed as:
explanation: Ohm's law states that voltage equals current times resistance (V = IR).

subject: Everyday Science
q: What is the SI unit of electric potential (voltage)?
explanation: Electric potential is measured in volts (V); one volt equals one joule per coulomb.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Which of the following is the best conductor of electricity?
explanation: Copper is an excellent conductor; wood and glass are insulators and steel is a poorer conductor.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Like magnetic poles:
options: Have no effect on each other
explanation: Like poles repel and unlike poles attract, the basic rule of magnetism.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The Earth's magnetic field protects life on Earth by deflecting:
explanation: The magnetosphere deflects charged particles of the solar wind away from the Earth.

subject: Everyday Science
q: An electric motor converts electrical energy into:
explanation: A motor converts electrical energy into mechanical (motion) energy; a generator does the reverse.

subject: Everyday Science
q: A generator converts mechanical energy into:
explanation: A generator converts mechanical energy (rotation) into electrical energy; a motor does the reverse.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Which is the nearest galaxy to our Milky Way galaxy?
explanation: The Andromeda galaxy is the nearest large galaxy to the Milky Way, about 2.5 million light years away.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Which is the brightest planet as seen from the Earth?
explanation: Venus is the brightest planet in our sky; it is called the morning star and the evening star.

subject: Everyday Science
q: A lunar eclipse occurs when:
options: The Sun comes between the Earth and the Moon
The Moon comes between the Sun and the Earth
The Earth comes between the Sun and the Moon
explanation: In a lunar eclipse the Earth's shadow falls on the Moon, so the Moon darkens.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The energy of the Sun is produced by the nuclear:
explanation: The Sun produces energy by fusing hydrogen nuclei into helium, releasing enormous energy.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Which is the most abundant element in the universe?
explanation: Hydrogen makes up about 75 percent of all normal matter in the universe.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Which element is most abundant in the Earth's crust?
explanation: Oxygen forms about 46.6 percent of the Earth's crust by weight.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Which is the most abundant metal in the Earth's crust?
explanation: Aluminium is about 8 percent of the crust, ahead of iron.

subject: Everyday Science
q: What is the chemical symbol of gold?
explanation: Au comes from the Latin word aurum, meaning gold.

subject: Everyday Science
q: What is the chemical symbol of iron?
explanation: Fe comes from the Latin word ferrum.

subject: Everyday Science
q: What is the chemical symbol of silver?
explanation: Ag comes from the Latin word argentum.

subject: Everyday Science
q: What is the chemical symbol of lead?
explanation: Pb comes from the Latin word plumbum.

subject: Everyday Science
q: What is the chemical symbol of tin?
explanation: Sn comes from the Latin word stannum.

subject: Everyday Science
q: What is the chemical symbol of mercury?
explanation: Hg comes from hydrargyrum, meaning liquid silver.

subject: Everyday Science
q: What is the chemical symbol of potassium?
explanation: K comes from kalium, the Latin name of potassium.

subject: Everyday Science
q: What is the chemical symbol of sodium?
explanation: Na comes from natrium, the Latin name of sodium.

subject: Everyday Science
q: What is the atomic number of carbon?
explanation: Carbon has 6 protons, so its atomic number is 6.

subject: Everyday Science
q: What is the atomic number of oxygen?
explanation: Oxygen has 8 protons, so its atomic number is 8.

subject: Everyday Science
q: How many elements are there in the modern periodic table?
explanation: The modern periodic table lists 118 confirmed elements.

subject: Everyday Science
q: How many groups are there in the modern periodic table?
explanation: The modern periodic table has 18 groups and 7 periods.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Who arranged the elements in order of atomic number?
explanation: Moseley arranged elements by atomic number in 1913; Mendeleev used atomic weight.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Noble gases belong to which group of the periodic table?
explanation: Group 18 holds helium, neon, argon, krypton, xenon and radon.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Which is the lightest element?
explanation: Hydrogen, atomic number 1, is the lightest element.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Which is the lightest metal?
explanation: Lithium is the lightest metal, with density about 0.53 g/cm3.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Which is the heaviest naturally occurring element?
explanation: Uranium (atomic number 92) is the heaviest element found in nature.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
explanation: Mercury is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Which non-metal is liquid at room temperature?
explanation: Bromine is the only non-metal that is liquid at room temperature.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Which of these metals floats on water?
explanation: Lithium, sodium and potassium are less dense than water, so they float.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Which metal is the best conductor of electricity?
explanation: Silver is the best electrical conductor, followed by copper.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Diamond is an allotrope of which element?
explanation: Diamond and graphite are both allotropes of carbon.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Graphite is used in pencils because it is:
explanation: Graphite is soft and its layers slide off, leaving a dark mark.

subject: Everyday Science
q: What is the molecular formula of buckminsterfullerene?
explanation: Buckminsterfullerene is a cage of 60 carbon atoms, C60.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Which of the following are the isotopes of hydrogen?
explanation: Hydrogen has three isotopes: protium (H-1), deuterium (H-2) and tritium (H-3).

subject: Everyday Science
q: Heavy water is chemically:
explanation: Heavy water is D2O, water in which hydrogen is replaced by deuterium.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Heavy water is used in nuclear reactors as a:
explanation: Heavy water slows down neutrons, so it works as a moderator in reactors.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Hard water contains dissolved salts of:
explanation: Calcium and magnesium bicarbonates make water hard.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Temporary hardness of water can be removed by:
explanation: Boiling drives off dissolved carbon dioxide and precipitates calcium carbonate.

subject: Everyday Science
q: What is the pH of pure water at 25 degrees Celsius?
explanation: Pure water is neutral, with pH 7 at 25 degrees Celsius.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The pH scale ranges from:
explanation: The pH scale runs from 0 (most acidic) to 14 (most alkaline).

subject: Everyday Science
q: An acid turns blue litmus paper:
explanation: Acids turn blue litmus red; bases do the opposite.

subject: Everyday Science
q: A base turns red litmus paper:
explanation: Bases turn red litmus blue.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Vinegar contains which acid?
explanation: Vinegar is a dilute solution of acetic acid, about 5 percent.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Citrus fruits contain which acid?
explanation: Citric acid gives lemons and oranges their sour taste.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Sour milk contains which acid?
explanation: Bacteria turn milk sugar into lactic acid, souring the milk.

subject: Everyday Science
q: An ant sting contains which acid?
explanation: Ants inject formic acid, which causes the burning pain.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Which acid is present in the human stomach?
explanation: Dilute hydrochloric acid in gastric juice helps digest food.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Which acid is known as the 'king of chemicals'?
explanation: Sulphuric acid is called the king of chemicals because of its huge industrial use.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Aqua regia is a mixture of hydrochloric acid and nitric acid in the ratio:
explanation: Aqua regia is 3 parts HCl to 1 part HNO3 and can dissolve gold.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Aqua regia can dissolve:
explanation: Aqua regia dissolves gold and platinum, which single acids cannot.

subject: Everyday Science
q: What is the chemical formula of baking soda?
explanation: Baking soda is sodium bicarbonate, NaHCO3.

subject: Everyday Science
q: What is the chemical formula of washing soda?
explanation: Washing soda is hydrated sodium carbonate, Na2CO3.10H2O.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Caustic soda is:
explanation: Caustic soda is NaOH, a strong alkali used in soap making.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Quick lime is:
explanation: Quick lime is CaO, made by heating limestone.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Slaked lime is:
explanation: Adding water to quick lime gives slaked lime, Ca(OH)2.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Plaster of Paris is:
explanation: Plaster of Paris is CaSO4.1/2H2O, made by heating gypsum.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Gypsum is chemically:
explanation: Gypsum is CaSO4.2H2O; heating it gives plaster of Paris.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Marble, limestone and chalk are all forms of:
explanation: Marble, limestone and chalk are all calcium carbonate.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Rust is:
explanation: Rust is hydrated ferric oxide, Fe2O3.xH2O, formed by air and moisture.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Galvanization is the coating of iron with:
explanation: A zinc coating protects iron from rusting.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Zinc protects iron from rusting because zinc is:
explanation: Zinc corrodes first, giving sacrificial protection to the iron.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Stainless steel is an alloy of iron with:
explanation: Chromium gives stainless steel its rust resistance; nickel adds strength.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Brass is an alloy of copper and:
explanation: Brass is copper plus zinc; it is used for utensils and fittings.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Bronze is an alloy of copper and:
explanation: Bronze is copper plus tin; it is used for statues and medals.

subject: Everyday Science
q: German silver contains copper, zinc and:
explanation: German silver has no silver at all; it is copper, zinc and nickel.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Solder is an alloy of lead and:
explanation: Solder (lead + tin) melts easily and joins electrical wires.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Duralumin, used in aircraft, is an alloy of aluminium with:
explanation: Duralumin is light yet strong, so it is used in aircraft bodies.

subject: Everyday Science
q: An amalgam is an alloy that contains:
explanation: Any alloy of mercury with another metal is called an amalgam.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Which alloy is used for heating elements in electric heaters?
explanation: Nichrome (nickel + chromium) has high resistance and a high melting point.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Bell metal is an alloy of copper and tin with:
options: A higher proportion of copper than bronze
A higher proportion of tin than bronze
explanation: Bell metal has more tin than bronze, which makes it hard and sonorous.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Gun metal is an alloy of copper, tin and:
explanation: Gun metal is copper, tin and a little zinc; it was used for guns and valves.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Oxidation is defined as:
explanation: Oxidation is loss of electrons (or gain of oxygen).

subject: Everyday Science
q: Reduction is defined as:
explanation: Reduction is gain of electrons (or loss of oxygen).

subject: Everyday Science
q: In the electrolysis of water, hydrogen gas is collected at the:
explanation: Hydrogen ions gain electrons at the cathode, forming hydrogen gas.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The volume ratio of hydrogen to oxygen obtained by electrolysis of water is:
explanation: Water is H2O, so electrolysis gives twice as much hydrogen as oxygen.

subject: Everyday Science
q: A catalyst is a substance that:
options: Speeds up a reaction without being consumed
explanation: A catalyst increases the rate of a reaction and remains unchanged.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Enzymes are:
explanation: Enzymes are protein catalysts that speed up reactions in living things.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Dry ice is solid:
explanation: Dry ice is frozen carbon dioxide, which sublimes without melting.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Laughing gas is:
explanation: Nitrous oxide, N2O, is used as an anaesthetic and is called laughing gas.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The main constituent of natural gas is:
explanation: Natural gas is mostly methane, CH4.

subject: Everyday Science
q: LPG (liquefied petroleum gas) mainly contains:
explanation: LPG is a mixture of propane and butane stored under pressure.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Marsh gas is the common name of:
explanation: Methane, produced in marshes by decaying matter, is called marsh gas.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Water gas is a mixture of:
explanation: Water gas (CO + H2) is made by passing steam over red-hot coke.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The gas used to ripen raw fruit artificially is:
explanation: Ethylene gas is used to ripen bananas and other fruit.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Carbon monoxide is poisonous because it:
options: Binds with haemoglobin and blocks oxygen
explanation: Carbon monoxide binds haemoglobin far more strongly than oxygen does.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Which gas is responsible for acid rain?
explanation: Sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides dissolve in rain to form acids.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Ozone gas has the chemical formula:
explanation: Ozone is a molecule of three oxygen atoms, O3.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The ozone layer protects life by absorbing:
explanation: The ozone layer absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation from the Sun.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Soil erosion is mainly caused by:
explanation: Running water and wind strip away fertile topsoil.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Which practice best prevents soil erosion on slopes?
explanation: Terracing and contour ploughing slow water flow and hold the soil.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Gypsum is used to reclaim:
explanation: Gypsum replaces sodium in saline soil and improves its structure.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Who is known as the father of modern chemistry?
explanation: Lavoisier named oxygen and hydrogen and stated the law of conservation of mass.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Oxygen was discovered by:
explanation: Priestley isolated oxygen in 1774; Scheele found it independently.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Hydrogen was discovered by:
explanation: Cavendish identified hydrogen as a distinct gas in 1766.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Which gas is filled in electric bulbs to protect the filament?
explanation: Argon, an inert gas, fills bulbs so the hot tungsten filament does not burn in oxygen.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The electron was discovered by:
explanation: Thomson discovered the electron in 1897 using cathode rays.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Avogadro's number is approximately:
explanation: One mole of any substance contains 6.022 x 10^23 particles.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Urea, the first organic compound made in a laboratory, was synthesized by:
explanation: Wohler made urea from ammonium cyanate in 1828, founding organic synthesis.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Sulphuric acid is manufactured by the:
explanation: The contact process uses a vanadium pentoxide catalyst to make sulphuric acid.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Ammonia is manufactured by the:
explanation: The Haber process combines nitrogen and hydrogen over an iron catalyst.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The main component of haemoglobin is:
explanation: Iron in haemoglobin carries oxygen in the blood.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Chlorophyll, the green pigment in plants, contains:
explanation: A magnesium atom sits at the centre of the chlorophyll molecule.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Which vitamin is ascorbic acid?
explanation: Vitamin C is ascorbic acid, found in citrus fruit.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The chemical name of 'soda ash' is:
explanation: Soda ash is sodium carbonate, Na2CO3.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Which acid is found in apples?
explanation: Malic acid gives apples their tart taste.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Which of these is a mineral acid?
explanation: Hydrochloric, sulphuric and nitric acids are mineral acids; acetic, citric and lactic are organic acids.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Which organelle is known as the powerhouse of the cell?
explanation: Mitochondria release energy from food by respiration, so they are the powerhouse of the cell.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Which part of the cell is called its control centre?
explanation: The nucleus holds the chromosomes and controls all cell activities.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Which organelle builds proteins inside the cell?
explanation: Ribosomes build proteins by joining amino acids together.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The cell was discovered by:
explanation: Robert Hooke first saw cells in cork in 1665 and named them cells.

subject: Everyday Science
q: How many chromosomes are there in a normal human body cell?
explanation: A normal human body cell has 46 chromosomes in 23 pairs.

subject: Everyday Science
q: How many chromosomes are there in a human sex cell (gamete)?
explanation: A gamete carries half the number, 23 chromosomes, so the zygote gets 46.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The largest cell in the human body is the:
explanation: The ovum is the largest human cell; it is just visible to the naked eye.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The smallest cell in the human body is the:
explanation: The sperm cell is the smallest human cell.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The longest cell in the human body is the:
explanation: A nerve cell can be over a metre long, running from the spinal cord to the foot.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The tissue that connects a muscle to a bone is called a:
explanation: Tendons are tough cords that join muscles to bones.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The tissue that connects one bone to another bone is called a:
explanation: Ligaments are strong bands that hold bones together at a joint.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The study of tissues is called:
explanation: Histology is the study of the microscopic structure of tissues.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The study of cells is called:
explanation: Cytology is the branch of biology that deals with cells.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The normal pH of human blood is:
explanation: Human blood is slightly alkaline, with a normal pH of about 7.4.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Blood is about what percentage of body weight?
explanation: Blood makes up about 7 to 8 percent of total body weight.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Plasma forms about what percentage of blood volume?
explanation: Blood is about 55 percent plasma and 45 percent blood cells.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The number of red blood cells in one cubic millimetre of blood is about:
explanation: There are about 5 million red blood cells in each cubic millimetre of blood.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The number of white blood cells in one cubic millimetre of blood is about:
explanation: White blood cells are far fewer than red cells, about 4,000 to 11,000 per cubic millimetre.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Platelets in the blood help in:
explanation: Platelets gather at a wound and start the clotting process.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The spleen is called the graveyard of:
explanation: Old red blood cells are broken down in the spleen, so it is called their graveyard.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The universal blood donor group is:
explanation: O negative blood has no A, B or Rh antigens, so it can be given to anyone.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The universal blood recipient group is:
explanation: AB positive blood has no antibodies against A, B or Rh, so it can receive any group.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The Rh factor in blood was named after the:
explanation: The Rh factor was first found in the blood of the Rhesus monkey.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The normal heartbeat of an adult at rest is about:
explanation: A normal resting heart rate is about 72 beats per minute.

subject: Everyday Science
q: How many chambers does the human heart have?
explanation: The heart has four chambers: two atria above and two ventricles below.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The largest artery in the human body is the:
explanation: The aorta carries blood from the left ventricle to the whole body.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The largest vein in the human body is the:
explanation: The inferior vena cava brings blood from the lower body back to the heart.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The valve between the left atrium and the left ventricle is the:
explanation: The mitral, or bicuspid, valve guards the opening between the left atrium and left ventricle.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The valve between the right atrium and the right ventricle is the:
explanation: The tricuspid valve has three flaps and guards the right side of the heart.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The natural pacemaker of the heart is the:
explanation: The sinoatrial (SA) node starts each heartbeat by sending an electrical impulse.

subject: Everyday Science
q: An ECG (electrocardiogram) records the:
explanation: An ECG traces the electrical signals that make the heart beat.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Normal blood pressure in a healthy adult is:
explanation: 120/80 mmHg is the standard normal blood pressure; 120 is systolic and 80 is diastolic.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The pulmonary artery carries:
explanation: The pulmonary artery is the only artery that carries deoxygenated blood, from the heart to the lungs.

subject: Everyday Science
q: How many bones are there in the adult human skeleton?
explanation: An adult has 206 bones; a baby is born with about 300, many of which fuse later.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The longest bone in the human body is the:
explanation: The femur, or thigh bone, is the longest and strongest bone in the body.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The smallest bone in the human body is the:
explanation: The stapes, a tiny bone in the middle ear, is the smallest bone in the body.

subject: Everyday Science
q: How many bones are there in the human skull?
explanation: The skull has 22 bones: 8 cranial bones and 14 facial bones.

subject: Everyday Science
q: How many vertebrae are there in the human spine?
explanation: The human backbone is made of 33 vertebrae, grouped as cervical, thoracic, lumbar, sacral and coccygeal.

subject: Everyday Science
q: How many pairs of ribs are there in the human body?
explanation: There are 12 pairs of ribs; the first 7 pairs are true ribs attached to the sternum.

subject: Everyday Science
q: How many cervical vertebrae are there in the human neck?
explanation: There are 7 cervical vertebrae in the neck of humans and most mammals.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The knee joint is an example of a:
explanation: The knee bends in one direction only, like a door hinge.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The shoulder joint is an example of a:
explanation: The ball and socket joint of the shoulder allows movement in all directions.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Bone cells are called:
explanation: Osteocytes are mature bone cells that maintain bone tissue.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Bone marrow produces:
explanation: Red bone marrow makes red blood cells, white blood cells and platelets.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Calcium and phosphorus are needed for healthy:
explanation: Calcium and phosphorus are the main minerals that build bones and teeth.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The strongest muscle in the human body by force is the:
explanation: The masseter, the jaw muscle, can exert the greatest force of any muscle.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The largest muscle in the human body is the:
explanation: The gluteus maximus, the main buttock muscle, is the largest muscle in the body.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Voluntary muscles are also called:
explanation: Skeletal muscles are attached to bones and move when we choose to move them.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The number of muscles in the human body is about:
explanation: There are about 600 muscles in the human body, making up nearly half its weight.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Muscle fatigue is caused by the accumulation of:
explanation: During hard exercise, muscles produce lactic acid, which causes tiredness and cramps.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Cardiac muscle is found in the:
explanation: Cardiac muscle is the special involuntary muscle that makes the heart beat.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The human brain weighs about:
explanation: An adult human brain weighs about 1.3 to 1.4 kg, around 2 percent of body weight.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The largest part of the human brain is the:
explanation: The cerebrum is the largest part of the brain; it controls thought, memory and voluntary action.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Balance and coordination of the body are controlled by the:
explanation: The cerebellum, at the back of the brain, keeps balance and coordinates movement.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The medulla oblongata controls:
explanation: The medulla controls involuntary actions such as heartbeat, breathing and swallowing.

subject: Everyday Science
q: How many pairs of cranial nerves are there in humans?
explanation: There are 12 pairs of cranial nerves, which arise directly from the brain.

subject: Everyday Science
q: How many pairs of spinal nerves are there in humans?
explanation: There are 31 pairs of spinal nerves arising from the spinal cord.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The basic unit of the nervous system is the:
explanation: Neurons are nerve cells that carry messages as electrical impulses.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The gap between two neurons is called a:
explanation: A synapse is the small gap across which a nerve signal passes from one neuron to the next.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The human brain uses about what percentage of the body's oxygen?
explanation: Although the brain is only about 2 percent of body weight, it uses about 20 percent of the oxygen we take in.

subject: Everyday Science
q: A reflex action, such as pulling the hand away from a hot object, is controlled by the:
explanation: Reflex actions are quick automatic responses controlled by the spinal cord, without waiting for the brain.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Body temperature is controlled by the:
explanation: The hypothalamus acts as the body's thermostat and also controls hunger and thirst.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Cerebrospinal fluid protects the:
explanation: Cerebrospinal fluid cushions the brain and spinal cord against shocks.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The human brain has how many hemispheres?
explanation: The cerebrum is divided into two hemispheres, left and right, joined by the corpus callosum.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Rods in the retina of the eye help us to see in:
explanation: Rods are sensitive to low light; cones work in bright light and detect colour.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Cones in the retina of the eye help in:
explanation: Cones in the retina detect colour and fine detail in bright light.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The blind spot of the eye is the point where the:
explanation: There are no rods or cones where the optic nerve leaves the eye, so that spot cannot see.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The iris of the eye controls the:
explanation: The iris opens and closes to change the size of the pupil and control how much light enters.

subject: Everyday Science
q: In the human eye, the image is formed on the:
explanation: The lens focuses light onto the retina, where rods and cones turn it into nerve signals.

subject: Everyday Science
q: In myopia (short sight), a person can see clearly:
options: Near objects, but not distant objects
Distant objects, but not near objects
explanation: In myopia the eyeball is too long, so distant images fall in front of the retina and look blurred.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The most common type of colour blindness is:
explanation: Most colour-blind people cannot tell red from green; it is more common in men.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The eardrum is also called the:
explanation: The tympanic membrane vibrates when sound waves strike it.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The cochlea in the inner ear is concerned with:
explanation: The cochlea turns sound vibrations into nerve signals that the brain hears.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The semicircular canals in the ear help in:
explanation: The three semicircular canals sense the movement of the head and help keep balance.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The number of taste buds on the human tongue is about:
explanation: There are about 10,000 taste buds on the tongue, most of which are replaced every two weeks.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Sweet taste is detected mainly at the:
explanation: Sweet taste buds are concentrated at the tip of the tongue.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The largest organ of the human body is the:
explanation: The skin is the largest organ, covering about 2 square metres in an adult.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Digestion of food begins in the:
explanation: Digestion starts in the mouth, where teeth chew food and saliva begins to break down starch.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Saliva contains the enzyme:
explanation: Salivary amylase (ptyalin) begins the digestion of starch in the mouth.

subject: Everyday Science
q: The largest gland in the human body is the:
explanation: The liver is the largest gland and the largest internal organ, weighing about 1.5 kg.

subject: Everyday Science
q: Bile is produced by the:
